items.raw_excerpt:
Now that Wikipedia has banned AI generated articles. - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Writing_articles_wit... I wanted to try and see if it was possible to get somewhat decent engine based on signs of AI writing from wikipedia themselves. It runs entirely in the browser via WASM. Added instructions to further add more ways to figure out as we find out more about LLMs. Would love feedback!!, especially:
- cases where it completely fails
- patterns you think are stronger indicators
- whether this approach is even worth pursuing vs proper ML models, considering this is a classical classification task, I just don't like the idea of detection of a black box with another black box.

"Such growth rates are rare in human history," says Xia Lixue, CEO of Wu Wen Xin Qiong, describing his most immediate impression of the current AI industry. Following the trend of "shrimp farming," the AI industry is undergoing an even more interesting shift: demand-side forces are reshaping AI infrastructure from the ground up. Consequently, token usage is skyrocketing, computing power supply and demand are mismatched, and system architectures are under pressure—issues once confined to the underlying layers are now becoming key variables in industry development. On March 27, at the 2026 Zhongguancun Forum Annual Meeting—AI Open Source Frontier Forum, a deep dialogue was led by Yang Zhilin, founder of Moonshot AI, with participants including Zhang Peng, CEO of Zhipu AI; Xia Lixue, co-founder and CEO of Wu Wen Xin Qiong; Luo Fuli, head of Xiaomi's MiMo large model; and Huang Chao, assistant professor and doctoral supervisor at the University of Hong Kong, and head of the Nanobot team. They discussed topics such as the current wave of intelligent agents and the evolution of AI infrastructure. As a representative of the infrastructure layer, Xia Lixue shared his observations and reflections on this round of AI transformation from the perspective of token supply and sustainable industry development. Token explosion: reminiscent of data traffic in the 3G era. In Xia Lixue's view, tokens are no longer just a billing unit but are becoming a fundamental production factor akin to "electricity" or "data traffic." He compares this phase to the early days of the 3G era. When mobile internet first became widespread, users quickly realized that a monthly 100MB data plan was far from sufficient.

Over the past two years, the leap in capabilities of large models has far outpaced the rate of change in corporate organizational structures. Abilities such as text generation, image creation, data analysis, and code writing have rapidly become accessible resources, yet the actual working methods within enterprises have not undergone a corresponding level of transformation. The reason is straightforward: the core activities of enterprises have never been about completing individual tasks, but rather about making continuous judgments in an ever-changing environment. Understanding markets, identifying opportunities, defining products, building brands, and driving growth—these activities form a continuously operating chain of decisions, not a one-time reasoning process. This is precisely why large models have not directly transformed enterprises.

From a longer-term perspective of technological history, enterprise software over the past two decades has roughly undergone three structural shifts. The earliest enterprise systems, such as ERP and CRM, were essentially process systems that reorganized corporate resources through standardized workflows, enabling enterprises to operate at scale.
